The most suspicious method is:

`com.google.javascript.jscomp.TypedScopeCreator.AbstractScopeBuilder.maybeDeclareQualifiedName(...)`

Why:
- The two `TypeCheckTest` failures both show the same symptom: after
  ```js
  Bar.prototype = { baz: function() { return true; } };
  Bar.prototype.__proto__ = Foo.prototype;
  ```
  the checker thinks `baz` is not defined on `Bar`.
- Statically, `maybeDeclareQualifiedName` has a special-case for assignments to `F.prototype`. If `F.prototype` already has a declared type, it returns early and ignores the RHS prototype assignment.
- For constructors with explicit `@extends`, `Bar.prototype` is already declared from the constructor type, so `Bar.prototype = {...}` is likely being skipped instead of merging/recording the object literal’s own properties (`baz`) onto the actual prototype type.
- That exactly explains why `this.baz()` becomes “Property baz never defined on Bar”, while inherited members from `Foo.prototype` are still a separate concern.

This also fits the third failure:
- In `testPropertyOnUnknownSuperClass2`, `Foo` extends an unknown superclass.
- Expected behavior is conservative: `x.getPropertyType("bar")` should be `?`.
- But actual behavior is `number`, which suggests the object-literal prototype properties are being attached too directly to the instance/prototype type even when the superclass chain is unknown, instead of keeping the result unknown.
- That points to the same prototype-assignment handling area in scope creation.

So the root cause is most likely incorrect handling of `Constructor.prototype = {...}` assignments in the scope/type creation phase, especially when the constructor already has an explicitly declared prototype/supertype.

m61.content:
The most suspicious method is:

`com.google.javascript.jscomp.TypedScopeCreator.AbstractScopeBuilder.maybeDeclareQualifiedName(...)`

Why:
- The two `TypeCheckTest` failures both show the same symptom: after
  ```js
  Bar.prototype = { baz: function() { return true; } };
  Bar.prototype.__proto__ = Foo.prototype;
  ```
  the checker thinks `baz` is not defined on `Bar`.
- Statically, `maybeDeclareQualifiedName` has a special-case for assignments to `F.prototype`. If `F.prototype` already has a declared type, it returns early and ignores the RHS prototype assignment.
- For constructors with explicit `@extends`, `Bar.prototype` is already declared from the constructor type, so `Bar.prototype = {...}` is likely being skipped instead of merging/recording the object literal’s own properties (`baz`) onto the actual prototype type.
- That exactly explains why `this.baz()` becomes “Property baz never defined on Bar”, while inherited members from `Foo.prototype` are still a separate concern.

This also fits the third failure:
- In `testPropertyOnUnknownSuperClass2`, `Foo` extends an unknown superclass.
- Expected behavior is conservative: `x.getPropertyType("bar")` should be `?`.
- But actual behavior is `number`, which suggests the object-literal prototype properties are being attached too directly to the instance/prototype type even when the superclass chain is unknown, instead of keeping the result unknown.
- That points to the same prototype-assignment handling area in scope creation.

So the root cause is most likely incorrect handling of `Constructor.prototype = {...}` assignments in the scope/type creation phase, especially when the constructor already has an explicitly declared prototype/supertype.

Best fix location:
com.google.javascript.jscomp.TypedScopeCreator.AbstractScopeBuilder.maybeDeclareQualifiedName(com.google.javascript.jscomp.NodeTraversal, com.google.javascript.rhino.JSDocInfo, com.google.javascript.rhino.Node, com.google.javascript.rhino.Node, com.google.javascript.rhino.Node)
